newsitem.title: UK: Brent's bull run far from over, say chart watchers.
newsitem.headline: Brent's bull run far from over, say chart watchers.

text.p: Oil prices, off the boil from six-year highs, could scale the heights again later this year and quash predictions that crude's long bull run is all but over, technical chart analysts said on Wednesday.

"Looking at an historical chart there is strong underlying support. We've had good basing action," said technical analyst Susan Rigg at Chart Analysis. "The potential for Brent to go higher is very, very good."
Front-month Brent futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange rallied $8 a barrel or 50 percent from the the end of May last year, hitting a post-Gulf War high of $25.06 on October 15.
Since then, a steady erosion of the gains taking Brent to a four-month low of $22 last week, has fuelled speculation that the bull run is finished.
Long-term chartists disagree. Many think Brent could rescale $25 before 1997 is out.
Cliff Green, technical analyst at Trend Analysis said $26 a barrel "could easily be achieved over the next quarter given the accumulated consolidation we've got so far."
"It should definitely have achieved that by the end of the year," Green added.
"We have an underlying constructive pattern which indicates we're at the mid-point of a bull trend."
Commodity markets tend to move in three stage cycles comprising a consolidation phase, a bullish phase and a bearish phase, Green said.
"We've emerged from the consolidation phase and we've seen some bullish action which the market is digesting," he said.
Green saw an ultimate goal over the next 18 months to two years of $30, in line with calculations off the base formed by price activity from 1991 to 1996.
He warned that Brent's passage to an interim $26 target could be choppy and that once it hit that level the market could undergo some severe corrective action as it processed the gains.
"This market can be fairly confusing because it's capable of correcting so seriously," he added.

Jake Bernstein, chartist and president of MBH Commodity Advisors in Northbrook, Illinois, also regarded Brent as being on a long-term uptrend, but said in the short-term it faced a further downward correction.
He expected Brent to remain bearish until the first week of May, during which time he said the prompt contract could drop to $20.
He predicted Brent, which was in the second year of a 10-year cycle, was on the path to $35-$38 in the next five years, near its lifetime $41 Gulf crisis high.
Rigg at Chart Analysts was also bullish in the long-term regarding price activity over the 1991-96 period as a good base for further moves higher.
But the market faced more consolidation before it could resume the uptrend, she said.
"It's in a funny phase at the moment and still has more consolidation to do," she said. "Breaks above previous peaks would be a good sign."
She expected Brent to stay in the $22-$25 range for the time being.
-- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7714.
